analyst.summary: Adani Green is India's biggest renewable-power generator and is genuinely executing well - it added more clean-energy capacity in FY26 than almost any company outside China and just crossed 20 GW operational scale. But the stock's price already assumes years of near-perfect growth, while the balance sheet tells a more stressed story: debt grew by nearly Rs 27,000 crore in a single year, interest costs are eating close to half of quarterly sales, and the profit-coverage cushion is razor-thin. On top of that, the company itself disclosed it lost Rs 1,200-1,500 crore of potential FY26 earnings because the power grid could not keep pace with the new capacity it built, forcing it to sell some power at a discount on the open market instead of at contracted rates. Governance risk has genuinely eased this year - the US bribery case against the promoters was permanently dropped in May 2026 and pledged shares are at zero - but at roughly 130-plus times earnings and 12.5 times book value, this is priced for perfection that a thinly-covered, still-heavily-levered balance sheet cannot comfortably guarantee. We rate it a Sell on valuation-versus-balance-sheet risk, not on the quality of the underlying business.
